source.title: Chapter 3: The Choice in the Storm

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The hold in near darkness, the whole image tilted hard. Plank shelves run along the hull, split into pens by upright boards, with four or five men seated or crouched in each; the other prisoners vary in age and build and wear grey, brown and off-white rags. The irons, fixed for the whole chapter: a rigid hinged iron collar with a ring at the side; wrist manacles joined by a short slack chain about a forearm long; ankle cuffs joined by a short hobble chain. Each pen has one chain. It runs collar to collar through the side rings, droops in slack loops along the plank between the men, and at the end of the pen rises at a slant to an iron ring bolted into the beam overhead, off to one side. No chain ever hangs vertical above a head. With the roll, bodies slide against one another and the pen chains jerk sideways along the rows. Nagoji is in the foreground pen, awake, one bandaged hand flat on the planks as if he were reading them. Nagoji per the captivity sheet: clean-shaven chin with light stubble at most, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, long curly black hair loose, no turban, torn ochre sleeveless tunic, cream dhoti, hands and wrists bandaged under the manacles, barefoot. A ragged flap of the torn tunic hangs over his left forearm, with grime and the wrist chain hiding it further; keep that forearm covered or turned from camera in every panel of this chapter.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first warning was not the shout of a sailor or the crack of thunder.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was the change in the way the ship moved.

panels.description: Close two-shot in the pen, Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, their faces a hand's width apart, both in collars and manacles. Keshavrao lock, as in Chapter 2: about nineteen, clearly younger, smaller and thinner than Nagoji; beardless apart from a faint youthful moustache; a rounder, softer face; narrow shoulders; black hair hacked short and ragged above the ears; a faded grey-brown torn knee-length tunic, never ochre; no ear stud; thin unbandaged hands; no facial scar. Keshavrao's eyes are turned up to the deck. Nagoji listens with his eyes half closed.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Storm.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ships speak when they are in trouble.

panels.description: Low angle up at the underside of the deck. Grey light cuts through the seams and water drips from them. Boot shadows cross the gaps at a run. Jagged, overlapping balloons come from above and off panel.

copy.speaker: SAILOR (off, above)
copy.text: Reef the sails! Haul, haul!

copy.speaker: SAILOR (off, above)
copy.text: Tie that down! Move, you son of a dog!

panels.description: The hatch is flung open onto a square of storm light, and a sheet of rain pours through before a canvas awning is dragged across it. A Portuguese ship guard braces himself at the top of the ladder, one hand on the frame and a flintlock musket in the other. The guard look for this chapter: lean, dark-bearded, a steel morion on his head, a soaked buff leather jerkin with a cross-belt over a shirt, as on the Chapter 2 guards; no key ring, no wide belt, not heavy, not ruddy; not a red coat and not a blue one.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: Quiet down there. No shouting. No prayers.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: If any of you break your chains and try for the deck, we put a ball in your gut and throw you over.

panels.description: Same angle, a heartbeat later. The ship lurches. The guard's foot slips off the frame and he pitches backward out of the hatch onto the deck above; only a flung hand and a boot sole show at the rim of the square of light. No guard enters the hold. The musket alone has left his hand and comes down end over end, clattering off the ladder rungs toward the camera.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It is easy to make threats on solid ground.

panels.description: Large. The musket in the foreground, spinning to a stop against a beam near the foot of the ladder, a few yards from Nagoji's pen. No guard in the hold. Behind the musket every chained head in the hold has turned to look at it. A lull in the roll leaves the pen chains hanging slack in their loops. Nobody moves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Muskets are like horses. They draw every eye in a space.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Even men who have never fired one recognise the shape of power.

panels.description: The hatch above. A second guard's head and shoulders are silhouetted there, the outline of his morion sharp against the storm light, as he shouts back toward the deck. He never looks down.

copy.speaker: GUARD 2
copy.text: Leave it! Get back to work.

copy.speaker: GUARD 2
copy.text: The pigs below are not our problem if the mast goes.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji (left) and Keshavrao (right), in collars and manacles. Keshavrao's eyes are on the musket and Nagoji's are on the hatch. Seawater is starting to thread across the boards past their bare feet and hobble chains.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Sahib, if the ship breaks...

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If the ship breaks, no musket will save them.

panels.description: Narrow strip at the bottom, at floor level. The musket lies against the beam with a thin current curling around its stock, and the ladder rises beyond it into grey light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Too far to reach. Too close to ignore.

panels.description: Wide, shot from a distance rather than in detail. The wave hits broadside. The hold is thrown sideways, men are almost weightless for a heartbeat, the pen chains snap sideways along the rows (never upward), and cold water surges across the floor to the knee.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The storm did not descend at once. It built in layers.

panels.description: Nagoji shouts down the line with both forearms hooked over the timber above his head, his manacled wrists together over the wood, taking some strain off his wrists and ankles. His collar chain droops slack to one side. Two or three men nearest him copy the grip.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (in Marathi)
copy.text: Hold to the beams! Hook your arms over the wood.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (in Marathi)
copy.text: Do not let the chain drag you.

panels.description: The ship rolls and Keshavrao, on the right, loses his grip. Nagoji, on the left, clamps his bandaged hand onto Keshavrao's forearm, and the chain between Nagoji's own manacled wrists swings and clangs against Keshavrao's cuffs.
Tight two-shot, Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, faces close, water streaming down them. Nagoji keeps his voice low, under the noise.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Storms break ships. When wood breaks, bolts pull out. Chains go loose.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The men above will think only of their own skins. There will be one moment when we can move without them seeing.

panels.description: Keshavrao alone (short ragged hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown tunic, iron collar), eyes wide in the gloom. A flicker of lightning through the seams of the hatch lights half his face.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Move where?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Towards air. Towards anything that floats.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: And if there is no such thing?

panels.description: Over Keshavrao's shoulder onto Nagoji. Spray bursts over both men as the hull groans. Nagoji has one manacled fist wrapped round the pen chain where it droops past him, jaw set, eyes level on Keshavrao. Behind him the plank at the end of the pen bows inward.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then we die here in the dark.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have seen the dungeon. That is what awaits us at the end of this journey. Tell me which death you prefer.

panels.description: Keshavrao, close (short ragged hair, faint moustache, softer young face, iron collar), water running off him: the ghost of a smile.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: With you, I prefer the one that involves a chance.

panels.description: Wide. Lightning through the gaps around the hatch cover freezes the hold in one harsh flash, like a portrait: men clinging to beams and to each other, mouths open, the whites of their eyes showing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The storm grew teeth.

panels.description: Looking up at the underside of the deck at the instant something heavy crashes onto it from above. The whole ceiling jolts, the planks bow downward under the blow, and sheets of water and grit pour through the seams. The hull timbers around the hold stay whole. Letter the first balloon before the impact (upper left) and the second after it (lower right).

copy.speaker: SAILOR (off, above)
copy.text: The mainmast! Cut the rope, it will take us over!

copy.speaker: SAILOR (off, above)
copy.text: She is taking water! Pump, for the love of God!

panels.description: Water pours in, surging waist-deep, and the chains drag heavy through it. A prisoner behind them gasps. Keshavrao, on the right, shouts into the ear of Nagoji, on the left, with his chin jerked upward toward the ring in the beam.

copy.speaker: PRISONER
copy.text: We will drown down here.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Look. The ring.

panels.description: Close on the iron ring bolted into the beam overhead, off to one side of the pen. The pen chain rises to it at a slant from out of frame below; it does not hang straight down. Dark cracks spread through the wood around the bolts and splinters lift at the edges.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: When it goes, we move.

panels.description: The ship drops away beneath them. In a spray of splinters the ring tears half out of the beam and now hangs from a single bolt. The chain's end drops and the whole length sags into the water, yanking the row of collars and wrists sideways.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A sound like a tooth being pulled from rotten gum.

panels.description: The prisoners cry out in wild, sudden hope. Nagoji rounds on them with his teeth bared.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Quiet! You want them to hear?

panels.description: Nagoji (left) and Keshavrao (right) grip the pen chain in their manacled fists and haul it level toward the camera, heels braced against the plank of the pen, timing the pull to the roll. At the far end of the chain the ring hangs on its last bolt. The pull is on their fists and shoulders; there is no upward pull on anyone's neck.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: On three. Pull as if you are trying to tear your own head off.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: One, two...

panels.description: The last bolt rips out of the rotten wood. The freed end of the chain whips loose and runs back out through the side rings of their collars, sliding away into the water between them; the splash is the line. They stagger apart, suddenly unmoored: each keeps his own empty iron collar, wrists still manacled and ankles still hobbled, and both look up into open space above their heads.

Wide. Nagoji and Keshavrao, each in an empty iron collar, work along the beam as far as their hobble chains allow, yanking at rings and kicking at the wood. One section's chain drops free. In the next, a ring sunk in sound timber will not give, and its men stare after them. Letter the two balloons at the left, at the start of the move.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Others.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Quickly.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Liberty was a generous word.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yet slack iron at the throat did something to the spine that torture had not.

panels.description: At the foot of the swaying ladder, thigh-deep, the musket a dark shape on the floor under the surface. Nagoji (left) looks up at the hatch; Keshavrao (right) looks at him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The hatch. We need air. We need to see.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: If we take it, they will shoot us.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If we stay, we may drown before they can load.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hands lift the musket clear of the water. The frizzen hangs open and the priming pan is dry and empty.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Sensible men do not leave a primed weapon lying about.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Still, weight is weight.

panels.description: Low angle up the ladder. Nagoji climbs with both manacled hands on the rungs and the musket jammed under one arm, knocking against the rungs; the hobble chain cuts every step short. Keshavrao waits at the foot of the ladder below him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Stay behind me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The ladder felt narrower than any siege stair I had ever mounted.

panels.description: Nagoji's point of view, looking straight up the ladder. A guard is already on the top rungs, coming down, backlit by a white flash of lightning: only a silhouette, the upturned brim and crest of his morion readable. One hand grips the ladder rail and the other swings the musket barrel down toward the camera.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: Back! Back, or I fire!

panels.description: Side-on and from a distance, both men small on the ladder against the lightning in the hatch. The ship lurches, and the guard's hand leaves the ladder as he loses his balance. Below him, Nagoji drives the musket butt upward two-handed into the guard's wrist, his wrist chain swinging, and the guard's weapon spins away into the dark. Do not show the injury close up.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Years of riding into gaps in enemy lines had trained my body to move before my mind could think.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Bone cracked.

panels.description: The guard falls past Nagoji, a dark shape between the rungs with his arms reaching for nothing. Nagoji presses himself flat to the ladder and does not look.
Looking down into the hold. At the foot of the ladder the current rolls a still, face-down shape against the planks like loose cargo, and the prisoners press back from it. No blood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The ladder was clear.

panels.description: Nagoji is at the top of the ladder, half out of the hatch, with rain hammering his back: empty collar, manacles, bandaged hands. He twists round to shout down into the dark.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Now! Move! All of you who can climb, move!

panels.description: About a third of the page, full width. The storm on deck: rain in sheets, the deck heeled over. The ship is the Chapter 2 vessel, hull black and high, her carved stern castle rising aft. The mainmast has snapped and leans at an angle, its torn canvas cracking like flags of surrender. The crew fight the weather everywhere: barefoot sailors in loose shirts and knee-length slops, some in knitted caps or head cloths, a mix of European, African and Indian men; some cut away rigging with knives in their teeth, others heave at the pump handles, their faces white in the lightning. No oilskins, no uniforms, no red or blue coats. Nagoji, just out of the hatch aft of the mast, has been thrown against the starboard rail and grips a line to keep from sliding into the black water; a coil of rope lies half loose at his bare feet. He wears his empty iron collar, wrist chain and hobble chain. Not one sailor is looking at him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The storm greeted me like an enemy who had been waiting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: To them I was just another piece of loose cargo tossed up from below.

panels.description: High angle from the hatch rim, looking down past Keshavrao as he climbs: his face turned up out of the hatch, eyes huge, his thin manacled hands on the top of the ladder, and below him in the shaft, lit by lightning, his bare ankles hobbled together on a rung. Short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, empty iron collar. The wind tears his voice away.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Sahib!

panels.description: About a third of the page, full width, looking to starboard on Nagoji's right. Nagoji small in the foreground, seen from behind, braced at the rail. A wave rears higher than the ship, a wall of water turned silver by lightning. Two insets along the bottom edge show what he takes in during the flash: Keshavrao's thin manacled hands clamped on the rim of the hatch, the wrist chain between them; and a shattered spar floating just off the ship's side.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Leap now, reach the spar. Keshavrao follows, chains drag him under.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Wait to free him, we both get smashed against the rail.

panels.description: Narrow strip. The crest of the wave curls over the rail and comes down, filling the panel.

After the wave, the deck awash in grey and white. Medium shot of Keshavrao, still clinging to the hatch, half in and half out, drenched, his short ragged hair slicked flat and a rain-washed graze at his hairline (no blood drawn); faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown tunic, empty iron collar. His left hand is clamped on the hatch rim. His right hand twitches at his side, reaching for a sword that is not there, the slack of the wrist chain letting it reach. Inset, upper left corner: Nagoji's bandaged, manacled fingers clawed into the rope coil on the streaming deck. The caption sits in the inset.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a moment I was nowhere. Only a body in a cold, roaring universe.

copy.speaker: KESHAVRAO
copy.text: Sahib! Do not leave me!

panels.description: Nagoji, on his knees on the tilting deck, heaves one end of the rope toward the hatch with both manacled hands, his face tight with effort. The throw lands short: the rope slaps wetly on the deck halfway across and its loose coils slide toward the scuppers as the ship tilts. Across the deck, Keshavrao lunges out of the hatch after it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had said, in the dark below, that he would follow wherever I jumped.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Tie it! Around your chest! Quick!

panels.description: Keshavrao, half out of the hatch, has the rope end in his manacled hands and is fumbling to pass it round his chest; the short wrist chain catches on it and his fingers are clumsy with cold. The rope runs back across the deck to Nagoji's hands at the edge of the frame. Over Keshavrao the next wave rears, its white edge already curling down toward the hatch.

Wide. The bow plunges into the next wave and the world turns to grey and white; the hatch is lost in it. In the foreground Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hands hold the rope as it snaps taut, his knee pinning the rest of the coil to the deck.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For an instant I thought he had managed it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That we would stand together on the deck and leap in our own time.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's palms as the rope tears through them. The bandages are scorched and stripped into trailing strips and the palms are reddened and burned; no torn flesh, no blood. Behind his hands, between them and the coil, the rope has parted at a frayed old splice, and the severed tail whips through his grip and out of the panel toward the rail and over the side. Under his knee the rest of the coil stays pinned to the deck.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then the line took the wrong kind of weight.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Keshavrao was gone.

panels.description: Wide and silent. The empty hatch, the broken ladder, water streaming into the hold, and no one there. Nagoji stands small on the deck in his empty collar, wrist chain and hobble chain, looking at it. His scorched, reddened palms are open at his sides, fingers trailing shredded bandage strips; the frayed end of the remaining coil lies at his feet.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The burns on my palms were the only proof he had been there at all.

panels.description: Tight on Nagoji's face on the right of the panel, rain running over it, his eyes still on the hatch: bare-headed, no turban, long curly hair plastered by the rain, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with stubble, gold ear stud, iron collar at his throat. From the left edge a memory seeps in like a stain rather than sitting in a clean flashback frame: Deccan riders galloping on past a fallen comrade lying still in the dust beside his riderless horse. The riders are anonymous, their faces lost in dust and shadow, and Nagoji is not among them. No blood. Letter the two captions over the stain, clear of his face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In the Deccan, before we rode into Portuguese fire, my troop and I had made a pact.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: If a man fell, the others rode on. We would mourn later, in camp, with liquor and song.

panels.description: At the starboard rail, Nagoji in profile. He has wound the rest of the rope twice around his chest and pulls the knot tight with numb fingers trailing shredded bandage strips, leaving the frayed free end to trail. Empty collar, wrist chain, hobble chain; the ragged tunic flap still over his left forearm. He takes one breath. Below and close, the spar rides the foam, splintered at one end, barnacles clinging to its underside.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: On the field there was no room for hesitation.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This was my field now.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Forgive me.

panels.description: The leap. Nagoji launches off the rail against a lightning-white sky, body stretched out over the black water, the rope trailing from his chest, wrist chain and hobble chain swinging, the ragged tunic flap still over his left forearm. The rail falls away behind him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: To the boy I promised not to leave. To the horse who died better than I would.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: To whatever gods listen to men who jump into storms.

panels.description: Wide, full width, the last panel of the chapter. Underwater, just below the surface, looking up past Nagoji as he sinks. At the bottom edge of the frame are his manacled hands and the rope knotted round his chest; the rope's free end snakes up toward the dark, barnacled underside of the spar floating above. The foam of his entry is a bright tear in the ceiling of water, and beyond it the ship's black, high hull heels away.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The sea closed over my head like the hand of an angry god.
